Naw, you're fine. You can still see the shapes in things you can see right? Just find the shapes the shadows make, the shapes the spaces around the object make, and then try to put them in-place to-scale on a piece of paper or canvas. It takes a bit to get the sizing right, but that's what the whole holding the pencil in front of you thing is about: you are measuring the size of something, and being like: "so it's like 3 of those", then you measure that thing on your drawing, and put your mark "3 of it" away.

Drawing is a lot of different things to different people. I know completely awesome artists who exclusively draw from real life or pictures. They literally cannot draw anything that is not already existing that they see in front of them, and they combine things into really unique compositions, successfully. I think practicing frequently is more important than most else.

Sorry if this doesn't belong this is more a question about culture and not directly a game. I'm not sure where else this would go.

Over the years, particularly this one, I've noticed a trend of harsh criticisms of games and game makers that don't have grounds. It seems like gaming has become so cool to talk about, that people will review games they've never played and circle jerk comment sections. I'm inclined to believe social networking has resorted in a degrade of it, due to the before mentioned circle jerking and click bait headlines. People won't click to read but will comment on the title (though this happens on many social networking sites). It seems like things were better back in the 90s and early 2000s. How do you guys feel about the gaming communities current state? Have people always done this in gaming and I just didn't notice?
Has social networking caused the gaming community / culture to degrade? What's your opinion on it's current state?

On a semi-related note, I want to talk about MiiVerse. Nintendo's own social network is honestly pretty cool for these exact reasons: It's heavily moderated and it promotes a more fun and upbeat user experience that honestly just makes even the social features of a Nintendo game feel even more Nintendo-y. I'm not a fan of censorship for the sake of it, but regarding Nintendo's built-in social network I can understand the why of it, and it does actually improve the whole "feel" of interacting with the console. Whereas, like OP says, coming on to the free-range internet to talk about games can often be like wading through a waist-high torrent of bile. And I will readily admit to being part of that bile in the past.

I'm anti-censorship too. I understand Nintendo's point to a bit as well, they have always aimed for more family friendly style of interaction and I feel like they do a good job of it. For a community that lets you draw, I've scene zero obscene pictures. Tons of cat and inkling memes. Nintendo stuff always feels like Nintendo. I would be against Nintendo's censorship if it was inhibiting discussion, but I feel like their miiverse is more like fun status updates not intended to get into heated discussions over or discuss anything in depth.

People are quick to jump on things in any community for good and bad reasons, be it in person or online. Social networking has only caused this to spread faster and amongst larger groups of people. In terms of your question about the impact of social media on the gaming community, I would say it is a double edged sword. Yes on one hand you can have harsh hate groups form over matters that at times they don't even understand. It hurts developers and players alike. But on the other hand you have this broader community to welcome new players, help them out and spread new games around. You need to weigh the positives to the negatives. I would say it has not caused it to degrade as a whole. It has just spread its reach in both positive and negative manners further.

As for the current state, I think its just an issue of the vocal minority when you see hate and misinformation being spread. Obviously it's not good to see, but it doesn't poison the whole community and culture of gaming.

Came here to say basically this. Also, I would add that hyperbole really gets attention. I think bashing is an easy way to get views, but isn't necessarily something with substance. Compared to when I gamed in the 90's and 2000's, I have way more information about way more games, and have benefited from it. Even if the information about the game is basically trashing it, sometimes it has an interesting effect of inspiring me to investigate further. There's good with the bad, but I think the net effect is positive.

Gaming communities are a blessing and a curse. On one hand, you can find new perspectives and secrets about games, share a laugh over something funny that happens in a game, or just get together to play a game. On the other hand, they raise the bar higher than lone gamers which makes them EXTREMELY critical of games that do not meet their standards.

I will say having grown up playing video games since the Atari 2600 and still gaming hard, it's good and bad. Yeah you do get some of the lazy journalism that other entertainment media has had to endure for years. One positive is that with social media you know have plenty of resources to help when you are stuck. Imagine trying to find all the Riddler's trophies without YouTube. With these gaming communities, you also have people to play with all the time. Try playing co-op with your incompetent friend or your younger sibling that keeps getting killed. With tha maturation of anything the changes come with good and bad.

Lol, but I feel like some of my more valuable bonding experiences came from those moments. You knew who your really good friends were cause they'd put up with you when you were sucking. You'd also train your younger sibling and watch them improve.

I think social media in gaming is more or less a double edged sword.

On one hand you've got interesting discussion of story, mechanics etc, means of helping other players,good word of mouth of interesting games, being able to share cool/funny moments and just really interesting opinions and perspectives of gaming.

While on the other hand you've got circlejerking, censor happy overmoderation, cynicism, hostiliy , corporate astroturfing and just all-round cuntery.

With the advent of social media in the gaming fandom I feel its probably brought out both negatives and positives and its probably very difficult to gauge which one is more prevalent than the other.
True, I suppose it's normal to notice more of the negatives over the positives.

I've been wondering the same thing.. Seems to me that my frontpage changes more frequently than mine did on Reddit.

The items are sorted by a score that depends on their age. On a large site like reddit, you cannot calculate this score for all submissions every time a user opens the page. So you have to cache it. That means it's less work but the result is going to be more static.

Reddit's ranking system has a bug that allows manipulation and effectively censorship: http://technotes.iangreenleaf.com/posts/2013-12-09-reddits-empire-is-built-on-a-flawed-algorithm.html I am not aware of this bug ever having been fixed, but welcome anyone to correct me if it has.
